before.title: 2.0L Turbo Wastegate Actuator Seizure Causing Boost Collapse / Limp Mode
before.description: On the base 2.0L 718 the single turbocharger and its electronic wastegate actuator are mounted low under the belly pan, exposing the actuator to road water, salt, and debris. Over time the actuator rod corrodes and seizes, so boost builds momentarily (e.g., ~15 psi) then collapses, or never exceeds ~5 psi. The result is sudden loss of power, juddery delivery under hard acceleration, and sometimes a PSM/engine warning; restarting the engine often temporarily restores boost. The 2.5L is less affected because its turbo sits higher in the engine bay. Porsche's official remedy for a failed actuator is replacement of the complete turbocharger; later parts have improved weather protection. This is distinct from the audible idle wastegate rattle in that it produces actual boost loss and turbo replacement.
before.solution: Diagnose with boost-pressure logging; freeing/greasing the actuator arm can be a temporary measure, but Porsche's fix is to replace the turbocharger assembly (under warranty/extended warranty where applicable). Use the updated turbo with improved actuator protection and inspect/seal the underbody exposure point.
symptoms: Boost builds then drops to a few psi

before.title: Air-Oil Separator (AOS) Diaphragm Failure
before.description: The air-oil separator in the crankcase ventilation system can fail, with the internal diaphragm tearing. This lets crankcase vacuum spike and draws engine oil into the intake, producing heavy blue/white exhaust smoke (often worst on cold startup or under load), oil residue in the intake tract, possible whistling/hissing from the engine bay, and lean/rich fuel-trim faults. Failures are documented on 718 flat-four cars, in some cases at very low mileage. Driving with a failed AOS risks oil consumption and, in severe cases, hydrolock/engine damage.
before.solution: Replace the AOS (some owners fit upgraded units, especially for track use); inspect the intake for oil contamination and clear any stored fuel-trim codes. Address promptly to avoid runaway oil consumption.
symptoms: Blue/white exhaust smoke, worst on startup or under load

before.title: Coolant Expansion Tank (Reservoir) Cracking at Seam Requiring Engine-Out Repair
before.description: The plastic coolant expansion/overflow reservoir on the 982 718 can crack along the seam where its upper and lower halves are joined, causing slow coolant loss that often only appears when the system is hot and pressurized. Forum discussion and a 982 service bulletin tie a higher incidence to cars built roughly March-August 2018; an integrated coolant-level sensor can also fail and trigger a 'refill coolant / stop driving' warning even when actual coolant temperature is normal. Because of where the reservoir is packaged, replacement on the 982 typically requires dropping the engine/transmission assembly, making an otherwise cheap part very expensive to address.
before.solution: Replace the coolant reservoir (and the level sensor if faulty) with the updated part; confirm whether the symptom is a true crack/leak versus a faulty level sensor before authorizing the engine-out labor. Pressure-test the system after repair.
symptoms: Slow coolant loss, worse when hot
'Refill coolant / stop driving' warning with normal temperature
Damp residue around the reservoir seam

before.title: Direct Injection Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
before.description: The 718 Cayman turbo flat-four and naturally aspirated flat-six engines use direct injection, which does not wash the intake valves with fuel. Carbon deposits accumulate on the intake valves over time, restricting airflow and causing rough idle, misfires, and power loss. The turbo engines are more prone due to higher intake temperatures.
before.solution: Walnut blasting of intake valves every 40,000-50,000 miles. Install an oil catch can to reduce the rate of carbon buildup. Chemical intake cleaning can help in mild cases but walnut blasting is the definitive solution.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes

citations.title: Planet-9.com — 718 carbon buildup walnut blasting intervals and DIY guide

communityRecommendations.content: Budget for walnut blasting every 40,000 miles as routine maintenance on any DFI Porsche engine — it is not optional, it is required maintenance.

before.title: Headlight and Taillight Condensation / Internal Lens Coating Defect
before.description: Moisture intrusion in the lighting units is a recurring weak spot on the 718. Owners report water droplets, pooling, or persistent fogging inside PDLS/LED headlights and in the taillights, even on low-mileage, garaged cars, attributed to imperfect housing seals. Separately, a defect in the headlight lens UV coating/material can cause fine cracks or a peeling/hazy film on the inside of the lens. Light venting mist that clears with the lights on is considered normal; standing water, pooling, or persistent heavy fogging indicates a failed seal and is sometimes replaced under warranty.
before.solution: Distinguish normal venting mist from true water ingress; for pooling water, persistent fogging, or internal lens cracking/peeling, replace the affected headlight or taillight assembly (warranty where applicable). Verify housing seals and venting are intact on replacement.
symptoms: Fogging or water droplets inside headlights
Pooling water in headlight or taillight housing

before.title: Manual Transmission 1st-to-2nd Gear Grind/Crunch
before.description: Owners of 6-speed manual 718 Caymans (including base, S, and GTS) report an intermittent grind or crunch when shifting from 1st to 2nd, most often on quicker shifts above ~4,000 rpm but also occasionally during gentle low-rpm shifts. Reported contributors include air in the hydraulic clutch line / poor clutch fluid condition, an improperly mounted or out-of-adjustment slave cylinder, and shift technique that doesn't let revs settle. In persistent cases owners have escalated to Porsche; most are managed without a gearbox rebuild, though a minority of 2.5 cars have reported needing transmission work for 1-2 grind.
before.solution: Bleed/replace the clutch fluid and verify the slave cylinder is correctly mounted and adjusted; confirm correct gearbox oil level/spec. Adjust shift technique (full clutch travel, let revs drop). If grinding persists after hydraulic service, have the dealer inspect the 1-2 synchros under warranty.
symptoms: Worse on fast upshifts above ~4000 rpm

before.title: Seized Ignition Coil Bolts During First Spark Plug Service
before.description: When the factory-fitted spark plugs are replaced for the first time (typically the ~4-year / ~40,000-mile service), owners and OPCs frequently find the ignition coil mounting bolts seized in place. The bolt must be drilled out and the coil pack replaced, turning routine plug maintenance into a multi-day, specialist job. Documented on 718 Cayman S cars; the repair has been covered under warranty after owner advocacy in reported cases.
before.solution: On the first plug change, anticipate seized coil bolts; if a bolt shears or seizes, drill it out and replace the affected coil pack. Use anti-seize on reinstallation. Owners within warranty should pursue coverage as a known defect.
symptoms: Seized/sheared coil pack bolt during spark plug service
Inability to remove coil for plug access
Extended shop time at first major service

before.title: Water Pump (Coolant Pump) Bearing/Seal Failure with Labor-Intensive Exhaust Removal
before.description: The engine-driven coolant pump on the 982-generation 718 four-cylinder turbo engines (2.0L and 2.5L) is prone to early bearing wear, plastic impeller degradation, and seal failure, sometimes as early as 20,000-40,000 km. A failing pump causes coolant loss and overheating risk, and because the pump is buried low in the mid-engine bay behind the exhaust, the catalytic converter / rear exhaust assembly must be partially removed to access it, driving labor far above a typical water pump job. A leaking pump can also damage the cooling system changeover (switchover) valve. Many owners and independent shops recommend proactive replacement around 30,000-50,000 miles / 50,000 km.
before.solution: Replace the coolant pump (often together with thermostat, gasket, pulley, and a coolant flush) once seepage, noise, or coolant loss appears; many owners replace it proactively before the warranty expires given the high labor content. Pressure-test the system afterward and inspect the changeover valve.
symptoms: Knocking, whining or squealing from the pump area

proposal.title: Water Pump (Coolant Pump) Bearing/Seal Failure with Labor-Intensive Exhaust Removal
proposal.description: Porsche bulletin 147/17 supports a coolant-pump leak condition on 718 Boxster/Cayman as of 2017: coolant can enter the pump vacuum area, an Engine Too Hot warning may appear, and affected vacuum lines plus the valve block/changeover valve must be checked before pump replacement. It does not establish bearing wear, plastic-impeller degradation, a 20,000-40,000 km onset, preventive 30,000-50,000-mile replacement or mandatory exhaust removal. Later coolant-pump parts-withdrawal records establish inventory actions, not field-failure prevalence.
proposal.solution: If an Engine Too Hot or stop-driving warning appears, stop and tow the car. Pressure-test the cold system, trace the highest leak point, verify circulation, and inspect pump-area vacuum lines and the valve block/changeover valve under bulletin 147/17 before replacing parts. Do not buy a coolant pump, thermostat, valve block, changeover valve, pulley or exhaust-removal service from this page; the leak path, failed component, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: highest leak point and circulation checked
pump, vacuum lines and valve block inspected separately
